statement: UNESCO documents Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove as an active Yoruba religious site with Osun shrines, continuing festivals and modern twentieth-century sculptural revivals, demonstrating documented ritual continuity alongside historical change at this particular place.

sources.citation: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove' (World Heritage 1118), Brief synthesis and Criterion vi, https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1118/
sources.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre / Nigerian heritage authorities
sources.access_note: Public UNESCO heritage account directly read. It describes active worship, annual festival and modern artists' interventions, with explicit distinction from earlier abandoned sacred groves.

does_not_demonstrate: UNESCO inscription in 2005 does not establish a founding date for Òrìṣà worship or Ifa.
Practice at Osogbo is a particular locality and is not a representative inventory of every Yoruba religious tradition.
New twentieth-century sculpture should not be misdated to precolonial ages.
adversarial_counter: Ongoing ritual use and artist-led restoration coexist; they require differentiated chronology rather than a static claim of unchanged authenticity.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
